items.title: AI suggests new physics experiments that could outperform human-designed setups
items.excerpt: Researchers report an AI system that proposes experimental setups for probing the laws of nature, generating designs that beat human-devised configurations. It shifts AI from analyzing results to authoring the experiment itself.

items.title: Hot subdwarfs come into focus as AI scans thousands of stars in Gaia data
items.excerpt: Vilnius University astronomers used machine learning to sift Gaia's catalog for hot subdwarfs — small stars that burn mysteriously hot for their size — turning a needle-in-a-haystack search into a survey-scale classification job.

items.title: System helps humans predict when self-driving cars will make mistakes
items.excerpt: MIT researchers built a method that teaches people where an autonomous system's competence breaks down, so human supervisors can anticipate failure modes instead of discovering them mid-drive.

items.title: Introducing WeatherNext 3, our most advanced and accurate global weather AI model
items.excerpt: DeepMind's new global weather model claims its most accurate forecasts yet, extending the run of AI systems that outperform physics-based numerical weather prediction at a fraction of the compute.

items.title: A connectomics milestone: Mapping the complete male fruit fly brain
items.excerpt: Google Research and collaborators completed a full synapse-level map of the male fruit fly brain, an AI-segmentation feat over petabytes of electron microscopy that gives neuroscience a second complete connectome to compare against.

items.title: An AI tool for prioritizing candidate biomarkers from wearable sensor data
items.excerpt: A generative framework mines continuous wearable-sensor streams to shortlist candidate biomarkers, aiming to turn consumer-device data into testable clinical hypotheses.

items.title: AI dominates the 4th International Congress of Basic Science in Beijing
items.excerpt: A dispatch from Beijing where AI took over the agenda of a major basic-science congress, with mathematicians and physicists debating what machine assistance does to the practice of discovery.

items.title: Live from ICM 2026: What Is Math For in the Age of AI?
items.excerpt: Quanta reports live from the International Congress of Mathematicians, where the field is openly arguing about what human mathematics is for once machines can produce and check proofs.

items.title: In an Age of AI, a Physicist Seeks What Endures
items.excerpt: A profile of a physicist asking which parts of scientific understanding survive when AI can generate predictions without explanation — a question about what counts as knowing.

items.title: AI agents aren't ready to replace humans in behavioral research
items.excerpt: New work tests whether LLM 'silicon subjects' can stand in for human participants in behavioral studies, and finds the simulated populations diverge from real ones in ways that would corrupt findings.

items.title: FDA pilot offers generative AI medical devices a path to patients before they are authorized
items.excerpt: The FDA's new pilot would let generative-AI medical devices reach patients ahead of full authorization, a regulatory experiment that changes how fast clinical AI can move from lab to bedside.

items.title: OpenEvidence launches new family of AI models
items.excerpt: OpenEvidence released a new family of models aimed at clinicians, pushing medical-literature reasoning tools deeper into everyday point-of-care decisions.

items.title: AI-assisted approach helps novice users capture heart ultrasound images and identify aortic stenosis
items.excerpt: Mayo Clinic tested AI guidance that walks people with no ultrasound training through capturing usable heart images and flagging aortic stenosis — expertise moved into the interface.

items.title: AI skin cancer detection tools are getting better, but only for people with light skin
items.excerpt: Melanoma-detection models keep improving on benchmarks while their accuracy stalls for darker skin, a training-data gap that turns a diagnostic advance into an unequal one.

items.title: Guidelines needed as AI embraced by mental health practices
items.excerpt: University of Queensland researchers found mental-health practices are already running AI for administrative work while lacking privacy, accuracy and governance safeguards.

items.title: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models
items.excerpt: Microsoft Research released efficient pathology foundation models designed to run over whole-slide archives at population scale, cutting the compute that has kept digital-pathology AI in pilot studies.

items.title: Explainable AI could help turn hidden data patterns into testable scientific hypotheses
items.excerpt: Researchers argue AI's value to science is not just prediction: the patterns models learn can be read out as new, testable explanations of how complex systems work.

items.title: Brain activity patterns could help sharpen LLM deductive reasoning
items.excerpt: A study uses human brain-activity patterns recorded during logical reasoning to steer LLM training, testing whether neural data can fix the deductive gaps text alone leaves behind.
